title: A `*` in a query sequence may build a profile position unlike HMMER's
body:
nail builds a profile from each query sequence in `Profile::from_blosum_62_and_seq` in `libnail/src/structs/profile.rs`. At each query position it takes the match emissions from the first 20 entries of row `residue` of `CONDITIONAL_PROB`, a 29 by 29 table. Since nail-de5410, a query fasta can hold `*`, which is code 27, so that position takes row 27. Nobody has checked what row 27 holds or what a profile built from it scores.

HMMER builds a query model the same way in `p7_Seqmodel` (`hmmer-3.4/src/seqmodel.c:62`), from row `dsq[k]` of its matrix `Q`. Nobody has checked what that row holds for code 27 either. `phmmer` runs with a `*` in the query. On the second record of `fixtures/target.fa` searched against the whole file, a terminal `*` left the top score at 1017.1 bits, and an internal `*` dropped it to 1010.8 bits.

## Proposal

Read what `Q` holds at row 27 in HMMER, and make nail build a `*` query position the same way.
close_reason: Landed in `8149a3b`. nail already built a `*` query position as HMMER does, from an all-zero row. The fix makes a zero probability add nothing to lambda's relative entropy, as Easel does. The comparison with `phmmer` is in the last note.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/87ab289b
notes.text:
HMMER builds a `*` query position from row 27 of its matrix `Q`. `set_degenerate_probs` sets that row to all zeros (`esl_scorematrix.c:1386`), `esl_scorematrix_JointToConditionalOnQuery` stops before it, and nothing renormalizes it afterwards. So the position matches no residue. nail's `CONDITIONAL_PROB` row 27 is all zeros too, and nail builds the same position.

The one divergence was lambda. `from_blosum_62_and_seq` summed `p * log2(p / f)` over every residue, and a zero `p` gives `0 * -inf`, which is NaN. Every hit then failed the reporting filter. Easel's `esl_vec_FRelEntropy` skips a zero `p`. With that change, `hmmbuild --singlemx` and nail both give lambda 0.78549 for `QDYCAQEGQQEVQRKDLSDLERYLRQSRQR`, with or without a `*`.

`util::relative_entropy`, which `adjust_mean_relative_entropy` calls, computes the same `0 * log2(0)` term. It was left unchanged here.

On the second record of `fixtures/target.fa` searched against the whole file, with null2 off in both tools, the top score was 1042.6 and 1042.5 bits for the plain query in nail and `phmmer`. It was 1042.6 and 1042.6 with a terminal `*`, and 1036.2 and 1036.2 with an internal `*`.
